title: Paclitaxel exposure in HCC1143: a compact single-cell evidence brief
question: Which cellular responses to a terpene-derived compound appear at 24 and 72 hours in one public single-cell experiment?

claims.text: Paclitaxel is a taxane diterpenoid, and GSE266934 includes HCC1143 single-cell libraries exposed to 1 nM paclitaxel or 0.1% DMSO for 24 or 72 hours.
claims.limitation: This chemical exposure experiment is not genetic Perturb-seq.

claims.text: After the prespecified cell QC, 1,106 and 788 cells remained in the 24-hour DMSO and paclitaxel libraries; 787 and 513 remained at 72 hours.
claims.limitation: These are filtered cells from one library per arm, not independent replicates.

claims.text: The treated-minus-control median interferon marker score was +0.218 at 24 hours and +0.510 at 72 hours; the selected cell-cycle score was -0.251 and -0.049, respectively.
claims.limitation: Scores summarize prespecified markers and are descriptive; they are not pathway activity estimates or statistical tests.

claims.text: Marker-level CPM ratios are heterogeneous: at both time points CCNB1 and UBE2C are higher in the paclitaxel library, whereas MKI67, TOP2A, and CENPF are lower.
claims.limitation: Pooled-library CPM can shift with cell composition, survival, and library effects.

claims.text: This four-library design has one library per treatment and time point, so it cannot establish biological reproducibility, cross-context transfer, or target dependence.
claims.limitation: The conclusion concerns evidence available from this particular design.

claims.text: Repeat the time-matched comparison across independent culture preparations, include a second dose and another terpenoid, and add a replicated target perturbation before testing target dependence.
claims.limitation: This experiment has not yet been performed.
